message.reasoning:
We need to generate unit tests covering many cases described. Use JUnit5, Mockito. Need to mock JsonSchema behavior for certain cases like external resource, fetchSubSchemaNode throws etc. Since JsonSchema is complex, we can use real factory for simple schema but for fallback cases we need to mock behavior of findSchemaResourceRoot().fetchSubSchemaNode etc. We can create a spy or subclass? Use Mockito to mock JsonSchema and its methods.

We need to create test class JsonSchema_getSubSchema_Test (already exists). We need to add more test methods for each group.

We must not modify @Before/@After. Use factory for simple schema.

For cases requiring custom schema with $id, definitions etc., we need to create schema JSON that includes $id in definitions. Provide schema string.

Also need to test numeric segment but parent not array.

Also test null fragment throws NPE.

Unsupported segment type -> need to create a JsonNodePath mock that returns Boolean segment. Since JsonNodePath is likely a class; we can mock it with Mockito to return nameCount=2 and getElement(1) returns Boolean.TRUE. Also getElement(0) returns "properties". Also getNameCount returns 2. Also need to ensure getNode(parentNode, segment) throws IllegalArgumentException. But getNode is protected method in JsonSchema; we can call real getSubSchema which will call getNode(parentNode, segment). The implementation of getNode likely expects String or Number; passing Boolean may cause IllegalArgumentException (maybe from JsonNode's get). We'll rely on that.

nullValidationContext: need to construct JsonSchema with null ValidationContext. But JsonSchemaFactory creates with proper context. Could use reflection to set validationContext field to null on a JsonSchema instance (since BaseJsonValidator has protected field). Use reflection.

fetchSubSchemaNodeThrowsRuntimeException: need to mock document.findSchemaResourceRoot().fetchSubSchemaNode to throw IllegalStateException. Since JsonSchema is not final, we can spy on a JsonSchema instance and stub those methods.

We need to import MockitoExtension? Use @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class) for mocking. Or use MockitoAnnotations.openMocks.

Simplify: For tests requiring mocking, we can create a mock JsonSchema (document) and stub methods. Use when(...).thenReturn(...). Use spy for root.

But getSubSchema uses findSchemaResourceRoot() to get document. So we can mock root schema's findSchemaResourceRoot to return a mock document. Use spy on root.

Implementation steps:

Create test class with @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class). Add tests.

Test 1: Successful navigation – array index segment

Create schema with "items": [ { "type": "string" }, { "type": "integer"} ].

Root = factory.getSchema(schemaString). Then fragment = SchemaLocation.Fragment.of("#/items/0"). Call getSubSchema, assert not null, subNode type string, sub.getSchemaLocation().getFragment() equals "#/items/0". Need method getSchemaLocation() - exists. Use sub.getSchemaLocation().getFragment().

Test 2: object property segment already done (existing property) already in provided test; but we can keep.

Test 3: $id resolution before final segment

Create schema with definitions address containing $id. Example:

{
 "$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
 "$id":"http://example.com/root.json",
 "definitions": {
   "address": {
     "$id":"http://example.com/address.json",
     "type":"object",
     "properties": {
        "street": {"type":"string"}
     }
   }
 }
}

Root schema = factory.getSchema(schema). fragment = SchemaLocation.Fragment.of("#/definitions/address/properties/street"). Expect sub.getSchemaLocation().getFragment() "#/definitions/address/properties/street". Also maybe sub.getId() equals "http://example.com/address.json"? Not needed.

Test 4: Segment numeric but parent not array

Use same simple schema with properties. Fragment "#/properties/0". Expect sub schema node for property named "0". Since property doesn't exist, getNode will return null? Actually parentNode is object with property "0"? Not present, getNode will return null leading to fallback error. To avoid fallback, we need to ensure object has property "0". So modify schema to include property "0". Example: "properties": {"0": {"type":"string"}}. Then fragment "#/properties/0". The segment is numeric? In JsonNodePath, the segment will be Number? The path parser may treat "0" as integer? Not sure. We'll mock JsonNodePath to return Number 0 as segment. Use Mockito to create JsonNodePath mock: when getNameCount returns 2, getElement(0) returns "properties", getElement(1) returns Integer.valueOf(0). Also getFragment maybe not needed. Then call getSubSchema on real root schema? Need root schema's getNode to accept Number segment but parentNode.isArray() false, so else branch used. Should work.

Test 5: Fragment not found – fallback returns null leading to InvalidSchemaRefException

We can use a root schema that doesn't have fragment. Then mock document.findSchemaResourceRoot().fetchSubSchemaNode to return null. To achieve, we need to spy root and stub findSchemaResourceRoot to return a mock document, and stub fetchSubSchemaNode to return null. Then call getSubSchema with fragment. Expect InvalidSchemaRefException.

Test 6: Fragment not found – external resolves successfully

Similar but stub fetchSubSchemaNode to return a JsonSchema mock that when getSubSchema(fragment) returns a stub sub schema. So root.getSubSchema should return that sub schema.

Test 7: Last segment without $id – sub-schema only at final step

Already covered by simple property age test. Provide test verifying that only final sub-schema created; but we can just assert that returned schema location fragment correct.

Test 8: nullFragment throws NPE

Call root.getSubSchema(null) expect NullPointerException.

Test 9: unsupportedSegmentType throws IllegalArgumentException

Create mock JsonNodePath where segment is Boolean. Use real root schema. Expect IllegalArgumentException.

Test 10: nullValidationContext throws NPE

Create root schema, then via reflection set its validationContext field to null. Then call getSubSchema with valid fragment; expect NPE.

Test 11: fetchSubSchemaNodeThrowsRuntimeException propagates

Mock document.findSchemaResourceRoot().fetchSubSchemaNode to throw IllegalStateException. Expect that exception.

Implementation details:

Need to import necessary classes: org.junit.jupiter.api.*, org.mockito.*, static org.mockito.Mockito.*, com.networknt.schema.*, com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode, java.lang.reflect.Field.

Add @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class) at class level.

Use @Mock for JsonSchema documentMock.

When mocking findSchemaResourceRoot, we need to stub root.findSchemaResourceRoot() to return documentMock. Since findSchemaResourceRoot is not final, we can spy root.

Example:

JsonSchema root = factory.getSchema(schemaString);
JsonSchema rootSpy = Mockito.spy(root);
when(rootSpy.findSchemaResourceRoot()).thenReturn(documentMock);

Set up documentMock.fetchSubSchemaNode(any()) etc.

Potential issue: findSchemaResourceRoot may be called multiple times inside loop; but the code uses document = findSchemaResourceRoot() initially, then later document.findSchemaResourceRoot().fetchSubSchemaNode... So we need documentMock to also have findSchemaResourceRoot() returning itself? Actually document is the result of findSchemaResourceRoot() on root. In fallback, they call document.findSchemaResourceRoot().fetchSubSchemaNode(this.validationContext). So document is root's resource root, which we mock as documentMock. Then document.findSchemaResourceRoot() should return documentMock (or maybe root?). To simplify, we can stub documentMock.findSchemaResourceRoot() to return documentMock. Then fetchSubSchemaNode behavior.

For test where fetchSubSchemaNode returns null, stub to return null.

For test where returns subSchemaMock, stub to return subSchemaMock; also stub subSchemaMock.getSubSchema(fragment) to return expectedSub.

Need to create JsonNodePath instance for fragment. Use SchemaLocation.Fragment.of.

Now write test methods.

Make sure to handle exceptions.

Now produce final code.
